# Risk memo: Tech heavy

_Deterministic template memo. Verified: 0 unsupported numbers, 49 figures traced to code._

## Summary

Tech heavy holds 6 positions (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META) and is compared with SPY. Between 2016-11-01 and 2026-10-29 it grew at 33.90% a year with annualized volatility of 27.95%, and its worst peak-to-trough loss was -45.07%. NVDA is 20.00% of the weight but 29.80% of the volatility.

## Return and risk profile

The Sharpe ratio is 1.08 and the Sortino ratio is 1.72, using a risk-free rate of 3.00%. The benchmark grew at 15.58% a year with volatility of 17.95% and a maximum drawdown of -33.72%. Beta to the benchmark is 1.33. The maximum drawdown ran from 2021-11-19 to 2022-11-03 and lasted 384 trading days in total. The effective number of independent risk bets is 5.26. Daily returns have skewness of -0.07 and excess kurtosis of 5.39; positive excess kurtosis means fatter tails than a normal distribution.

## Tail risk

On a typical bad day (1-day, 95% confidence, historical) the portfolio loses at least 2.93%, and the average loss on those days is 4.10%. At 99% confidence the historical VaR is 4.85% and the Expected Shortfall 6.05%, against a normal-distribution VaR of 4.10%. The 10-day 95% historical VaR is 7.72%. In a rolling backtest the 95% historical VaR was exceeded on 122 days against 113.2 expected (Kupiec verdict: consistent); at 99% the verdict is model underestimates risk. Over the next 252 trading days, a simulation assuming 5.00% annual drift gives a 47.15% chance of a loss, a median return of 1.89% and a 65.89% chance of a drawdown deeper than one fifth of value.

## Stress and regimes

Of 4 historical stress scenarios with enough history, the worst was 2022 rate shock: the portfolio returned -40.49% against -24.50% for the benchmark. A regime model on the benchmark puts the market in a Calm regime (90.37% probability); in Stress regimes this portfolio's volatility is 4.5x its Calm level. In a walk-forward volatility test the best forecaster was GARCH-t, which forecasts annualized volatility of 25.42% for the next month.

## Disclosed risks from filings

- Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) discloses a risk in its 10-K. ([META 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828026003942/meta-20251231.htm))
- Apple Inc. (AAPL) discloses a risk in its 10-K. ([AAPL 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019325000079/aapl-20250927.htm))
- AMAZON COM INC (AMZN) discloses a risk in its 10-K. ([AMZN 10-K FY2025, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000004/amzn-20251231.htm))
- MICROSOFT CORP (MSFT) discloses a risk in its 10-K. ([MSFT 10-K FY2026, Item 1A](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526323660/msft-20260630.htm))

## Caveats and limitations

- All figures are historical estimates from daily data between 2016-11-01 and 2026-10-29; future losses can be larger.
- Value at Risk and Expected Shortfall assume the past is representative of the future; the normal-distribution versions understate fat tails.
- Monte Carlo results depend on the assumed annual return of 5.00% and resample past daily returns.
- Regimes come from a hidden Markov model fitted to the benchmark; the current regime uses only data up to the last date.
- Disclosed risks summarize the latest 10-K risk factors; ETFs and funds have none.

_Educational tool, not investment advice. Models are simplifications; historical risk measures can understate future losses._
